name: Historic Center (Corso Umberto)
description: The pedestrian core strung along Corso Umberto, from the Teatro Antico to the Piazza IX Aprile terrace. Bougainvillea-draped lanes, boutiques, trattorias and panoramic viewpoints define daily life here, with Etna and the sea always in frame. Beautiful, central and steep.
bestFor: Culture-first slow travelers wanting the classic Taormina experience
pros: Walk everywhere among the town's best sights and dining
Spectacular views of Etna and the Ionian Sea
Lively year-round core with cafes and easy wifi stays
cons: Priciest area and mobbed in high summer
Steep staircases and lanes, tough with luggage

name: Isola Bella / Mazzaro
description: The seafront zone directly below Taormina, linked to the center by the funivia cable car. Home to the pebbly Mazzaro beach and the tiny Isola Bella islet nature reserve, it offers swimming, snorkeling and waterfront dining a short ride from the hilltop bustle.
bestFor: Beach lovers wanting sea access with town nearby
pros: Direct access to beaches and the Isola Bella reserve
Cable car whisks you up to the center in minutes
Calmer, waterfront atmosphere away from the crush
cons: Limited flat walking and pricey beachfront stays
Cable car queues and closures can strand you

name: Giardini Naxos
description: A bigger, more down-to-earth seaside resort in the bay just below Taormina, built on the site of Sicily's first Greek colony. It offers longer sandy-pebble beaches, more affordable stays and everyday amenities, with easy buses up to the hilltop town.
bestFor: Budget-conscious slow travelers wanting beach and value
pros: Noticeably cheaper rentals than the hilltop center
Long seafront promenade with beaches and restaurants
Good bus and train links to Taormina and Catania
cons: Less charm and glamour than Taormina proper
You will commute up for the marquee sights

name: Castelmola
description: A minuscule medieval hamlet perched above Taormina, crowned by castle ruins and famous for even higher, sweeping views over the town, Etna and the coast. Quiet, atmospheric and reachable by a short drive or bus, it makes a peaceful, panoramic base for a slow stay.
bestFor: Peace-seekers wanting the best views and calm
pros: Unbeatable panoramas over Taormina, Etna and the sea
Quiet, authentic village atmosphere and cheaper stays
Charming lanes, cafes and its almond-wine tradition
cons: Isolated and reliant on driving or infrequent buses
Very few amenities and limited nightlife or dining
